trusted_publishers.rationale: Trust the Tor Project Arti release maintainer for these 36 explicitly enumerated client/protocol packages from official Arti 2.8.0. Tor lists Gabi on its Arti Network Team; her official Tor key fingerprint matches the gabi-250 GitHub profile, crates.io maps that exact GitHub identity to user 31201, and the official release tag names every package/version and resolves to their packaged VCS commit. The pinned README supports general client usage. Trust includes adversarial Tor cells, certificates and directory parsing, cryptographic and memory/unsafe invariants, circuit isolation, filesystem keystores and concurrency, beyond safe compilation. It is maintainer trust, not an independent cryptographic/privacy proof or approval of experimental relay features.

new_agent_audits.name: strum
new_agent_audits.notes: Reviewed both manifests, complete src/lib.rs and the documentation-only additional_attributes.rs, README and package inventory. The crate defines safe trait interfaces/constants and a fixed ParseError formatter; all user-supplied strings are passed as data to formatting. The only macro emits cfg-gated reexports of a finite identifier list. No unsafe code, build script, native component, filesystem/process/network access or generated pointer manipulation. Optional strum_macros and phf are only reexports and require independent safe-to-deploy coverage; this audit does not certify their generated implementations. In an isolated archive copy with only an empty workspace marker added and netd lock resolution seeded, offline all-feature cargo test compiled and passed four doctests, with zero unit tests. The procedural macro implementation remains a separate explicit gap.

new_agent_audits.name: displaydoc
new_agent_audits.notes: Reviewed both manifests and all production modules: lib.rs, attr.rs, expand.rs and fmt.rs, including both std/no_std expansion branches, shorthand parsing and generic bounds. No build script, unsafe, native component or ambient I/O. Doc text is retained as syn::LitStr; identifiers use checked character classes and compiler token types, never eval, a shell or a parsed arbitrary expression. Brace slicing uses ASCII byte positions from find; identifier slicing uses char_indices. Malformed or unsupported attributes may panic during compilation or produce diagnostics, not runtime execution of doc text. Generated code destructures a shared borrow, adds core::fmt::Display bounds, emits ordinary write! calls and safe borrowed Path display helpers; it introduces no unsafe impl or unchecked lifetime extension. Empty-enum unreachable! is not reachable by a safely constructed value. Formatting intentionally exposes values selected by the caller: NymWrap must retain its content-free logging policy. Dependencies syn/quote/proc-macro2 remain separately accountable. The full upstream offline test command was blocked by an uncached pretty_assertions dev dependency and ran no tests. A separate dependency-only harness used three unmodified upstream integration test files: std mode passed three tests, no-default-features passed two, and the no_std target compiled in both. Other upstream unit/UI/doctests were not run.

findings.name: convert_case
findings.severity: Unrated; audit-blocking panic in custom-boundary API, no NymWrap exploitability claim.
findings.criterion_decision: No safe-to-deploy audit or publisher trust added.
findings.mechanism: split visits each grapheme even after consuming a multi-grapheme delimiter. The overlapping match begins before last_boundary_end; slicing s[last_boundary_end..boundary_byte_start] panics. The ordinary a::b case succeeds.

reproduction.assertion: The probe uses catch_unwind and asserts that the exact trigger panics; successful exit confirms reproduction, not safety.
